1	# Distributed Operators (N6)
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	The N6 distributed op family gives the Python DSL direct, typed access to the
6	hardware's cross-rank communication primitives. Every op operates against a
7	**window-bound** [`DistributedTensorType`](ir/02-types.md) — a tensor whose
8	storage is a slice of a symmetric, per-rank communication window allocated by
9	`pld.alloc_window_buffer`. Verifiers in this family generally reject plain
10	`TensorType` (strict kind-trait matching — `As<DistributedTensorType>` does
11	not match a plain `TensorType`), so a non-window-bound tensor can never be fed
12	into a cross-rank slot by accident. **Two documented exceptions**, both matched
13	via `AsTensorTypeLike` and detailed under Namespacing below: `put`/`tile.put`
14	accept a plain `Tensor` as `src`, and `get`/`tile.get` accept one as `dst` —
15	TPUT/TGET only need a readable/writable *local* GM region on that side. The
16	window-bound side (`put.dst`, `get.src`) still requires a `DistributedTensor`.
17	
18	There are **fifteen ops** and **four ABI enums**:
19	
20	| Op | Direction | Result | Hardware |
21	| -- | --------- | ------ | -------- |
22	| `pld.tile.remote_load` | pull (read peer → local tile) | `TileType` | TLOAD |
23	| `pld.tile.remote_store` | push (write local tile → peer) | `Unknown` (side effect) | TSTORE |
24	| `pld.tensor.remote_store` | push (write local tensor-level value → peer); lowered 1:1 to `pld.tile.remote_store` | `Unknown` (side effect) | TSTORE |
25	| `pld.tensor.get` | pull (read peer → local GM) | `Unknown` (side effect) | TGET |
26	| `pld.tensor.put` | push (write local → peer) | `Unknown` (side effect) | TPUT |
27	| `pld.tensor.allreduce` | collective reduce over window slices | `DistributedTensorType` (same as src) | builtin collective |
28	| `pld.tensor.barrier` | synchronise visibility of window data across ranks | `DistributedTensorType` (same as src) | builtin collective |
29	| `pld.tensor.broadcast` | replicate root rank's data to all ranks | `DistributedTensorType` (same as src) | builtin collective |
30	| `pld.tensor.reduce_scatter` | reduce and scatter chunks across ranks | `DistributedTensorType` (same as src) | builtin collective |
31	| `pld.tensor.allgather` | gather data from all ranks via window | `DistributedTensorType` (same as src) | builtin collective |
32	| `pld.tensor.all_to_all` | push-based symmetric personalized exchange — every rank pushes its per-destination chunks to every peer's window via `pld.tensor.put` (TPUT), returns window as result | `DistributedTensorType` (same as src) | composite / HOST builtin |
33	| `pld.tensor.all_to_all_v` | variable-size all-to-all (MPI_Alltoallv) — pushes the full MAX_RECV-row block per destination into a flat 2D staging window (transfer size is the full per-destination capacity block), and publishes `min(send_counts[dest], MAX_RECV)` into peer `recv_counts[my_rank, 0]` via `pld.system.notify` (Set) so the receiver can skip rows beyond its count; returns window as result (same window-as-result pattern as symmetric `all_to_all`) | `DistributedTensorType` (same as target) | composite / HOST builtin |
34	| `pld.system.notify` | signal a peer's slot | `Unknown` (side effect) | TNOTIFY |
35	| `pld.system.wait` | block on own slot | `Unknown` (side effect) | TWAIT |
36	| `pld.system.defer_wait` | defer this task's logical completion on a local counter | `Unknown` (side effect) | Simpler completion runtime (no PTOAS wait op) |
37	
38	The seven side-effect-only ops produce [`UnknownType`](ir/02-types.md): they
39	exist for their cross-rank effect, not for an SSA value a consumer reads.
40	
41	## Namespacing: why `tile.*` vs `tensor.*` vs `system.*`
42	
43	The namespace encodes the IR level the op lives at, not an arbitrary grouping:
44	
45	- **`pld.tile.remote_load`** produces a *tile* (on-core SRAM region), so it is a
46	  sibling of `tile.load` and lives in `pld.tile`.
47	- **`pld.tile.remote_store`** consumes a *tile* (the symmetric write companion
48	  of `remote_load`), so it is a sibling of `tile.store` and lives in
49	  `pld.tile`.
50	- **`pld.tensor.remote_store`** is the same op one IR level up — it consumes a
51	  *tensor-level* value, so it lives in `pld.tensor` and `ConvertTensorToTileOps`
52	  lowers it 1:1 to `pld.tile.remote_store`. This is the `tensor.aiv_shard` /
53	  `tile.aiv_shard` shape (**one op, two levels, one identical argument
54	  surface**), and it is why the tensor-level push is a separate entry point
55	  rather than an overload of `pld.tensor.put`: dispatching `put` on the kind of
56	  its `src` would make five of its arguments (`src_offsets`, `shape`, `atomic`,
57	  `chunk_*`, `pipeline`) conditionally meaningless depending on how the value
58	  was produced upstream — a property invisible at the call site.
59	- **`pld.tensor.get` / `pld.tensor.put`** read and write *tensor* (GM) operands
60	  on both sides. The window-bound side is the one the peer needs a slot for
61	  (`get.src`, `put.dst`); the local side (`get.dst`, `put.src`) also accepts a
62	  plain `Tensor`, so kernels can TGET into / TPUT from host-backed tensors
63	  without staging through a window buffer. The VEC staging tile they bounce
64	  through is materialised by `ConvertTensorToTileOps` as an internal
65	  `pld.tile.get` / `pld.tile.put`, never on the DSL surface. Both are therefore
66	  siblings of `pld.tensor.alloc_window_buffer` / `pld.tensor.window`, **not** of
67	  the tile-producing `remote_load`.
68	- **`pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait` / `pld.system.defer_wait`** drive
69	  the per-rank signal slot — pure control-plane synchronisation with no data
70	  operand — so they live in `pld.system`. `wait` blocks and later resumes its
71	  kernel; `defer_wait` returns and transfers readiness to the scheduler TaskId.
72	
73	## Core placement in a mixed kernel
74	
75	`ExpandMixedKernel` splits a mixed InCore function into an AIC and an AIV
76	function using `core_affinity::ClassifyCallAffinity`. Statements that classify
77	`SHARED` are **duplicated onto both lanes**, so every distributed op has to be
78	explicit about two independent questions: *which* core may run it, and *how many
79	times* it may run.
80	
81	| Op | Affinity | Why |
82	| -- | -------- | --- |
83	| `pld.tile.put` / `pld.tensor.put`, `pld.tile.get` / `pld.tensor.get` | `VECTOR` (declared) | TPUT/TGET stream GM → UB → remote GM through a VEC staging tile; ptoas enforces it (`verifyCommStagingTileLike` requires `AddressSpace::VEC`). The tile forms would classify VECTOR incidentally via their staging-tile operand; the tensor forms have no tile operand and would otherwise be duplicated onto the cube lane |
84	| `pld.tile.remote_store` | derived: VECTOR | Inherits VECTOR from its source tile operand via the first-tile-argument rule |
85	| `pld.tile.remote_load` | `SHARED` (**known gap**) | Its tile is the *result*, not an argument, and it declares no memory spec — so both memory rules miss it and it reaches the `SHARED` fallback, which `ExpandMixedKernel` replicates onto both lanes. Benign today: the cube copy produces a `Vec` tile no cube statement consumes, so DCE removes it. Not fixed by declaring VECTOR (a false ISA claim — the destination could be a cube-side buffer) nor by classifying from the result tile: `LowerAutoVectorSplit` treats a VECTOR-affine leaf as "halve this", and the halving path has no rewrite for the op's `offsets` / `shape` tuples. A real fix teaches the halving path about the op |
86	| `pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait` | `SHARED` (deliberately undeclared) | Their pto-isa implementations are pure scalar/GM (`st_atomic`, `dcci`, `dsb`) and ptoas imposes no core or section constraint — pto-isa's own cube-built `allgather_gemm_compute_kernel.cpp` calls TWAIT. Declaring VECTOR here would be a false claim about the ISA |
87	
88	`pld.system.notify` additionally carries the registry's `set_no_duplicate()`
89	flag — for **both** `NotifyOp` forms. The hazard on the cube lane is not
90	double-counting but **premature release from the wrong lane**: the AIC copy can
91	publish the signal before the AIV lane's TPUT has landed the data that signal
92	releases, so the peer reads stale bytes. A `NotifyOp::kSet` fires that race
93	exactly as readily as an atomic-add.
94	
95	`pld.system.wait` is deliberately left unmarked, and not because TWAIT is
96	idempotent: it *blocks*, and its presence on the cube lane is load-bearing —
97	pinning it to the vector lane would let the matmul race past the peer data it
98	waits on.
99	
100	The flag is orthogonal to affinity (it constrains replication, not placement).
101	Its only consumer is `LowerAutoVectorSplit`'s `pl.split_aiv` region placement
102	stamp, which pins a region's no-duplicate calls to the AIV lane; see
103	`docs/en/dev/ir/05-operators.md` and
104	`docs/en/dev/passes/20-lower_auto_vector_split.md`.
105	
106	**Comm ops written outside every region are still duplicated onto both lanes,
107	and nothing diagnoses it.** Putting the comm phase in a `pl.split_aiv` region is
108	the author's job; see `docs/en/user/language/04-scopes.md`.
109	
110	## ABI enums (`include/pypto/ir/comm.h`)
111	
112	The four enums are an **append-only ABI**. Their underlying `int` values are
113	serialised as the op's kwarg payload (`op` for notify, `cmp` for wait/defer_wait, `atomic`
114	for put) and cast back to the enum at codegen time. New variants may only be
115	added **at the end** so existing IR and cached programs keep their meaning.
116	
117	```cpp
118	enum class NotifyOp : int { kAtomicAdd = 0, kSet = 1 };   // pld.system.notify
119	enum class WaitCmp  : int { kEq = 0,        kGe = 1 };     // pld.system.wait / defer_wait
120	enum class AtomicType : int { kNone = 0,    kAdd = 1 };    // pld.tensor.put, remote_store
121	enum class ReduceOp : int { kSum = 0, kMax = 1, kMin = 2, kProd = 3 };  // pld.tensor.allreduce
122	```
123	
124	| Enum | Variant | Meaning |
125	| ---- | ------- | ------- |
126	| `NotifyOp` | `kAtomicAdd` | atomically add `value` into the peer's signal slot |
127	| `NotifyOp` | `kSet` | non-atomic store of `value` into the peer's signal slot |
128	| `WaitCmp` | `kEq` | block until `*signal_slot == expected` |
129	| `WaitCmp` | `kGe` | wait, or defer task completion, until `*signal_slot >= expected` |
130	| `AtomicType` | `kNone` | plain remote store — overwrite the peer's dst slice |
131	| `AtomicType` | `kAdd` | atomically add the source data into the peer's dst slice |
132	| `ReduceOp` | `kSum` | sum-reduce every participating rank's window slice |
133	| `ReduceOp` | `kMax` | max-reduce every participating rank's window slice |
134	| `ReduceOp` | `kMin` | min-reduce every participating rank's window slice |
135	| `ReduceOp` | `kProd` | product-reduce every participating rank's window slice |
136	
137	Each enum is mirrored across three layers (C++ `enum class` → `nb::enum_` in the
138	bindings → `.pyi` stub) and surfaced to the DSL as `pld.NotifyOp` /
139	`pld.WaitCmp` / `pld.AtomicType` / `pld.ReduceOp`. The deducer validates the packed `int`
140	against the enum range so codegen can cast back without a second guard.
141	
142	## Barrier-signal protocol
143	
144	Every `pld.tensor.*` collective (`allreduce`, `barrier`, `broadcast`,
145	`reduce_scatter`, `allgather`, `all_to_all`, `all_to_all_v`) synchronises through one shared,
146	**self-clearing credit barrier** built from `pld.system.notify` /
147	`pld.system.wait`:
148	
149	```text
150	Body:      barrier(1); barrier(2); ...; barrier(N)   # g counted within this
151	                                                      # call only
152	  barrier(g):
153	    for peer != my_rank: notify(signal, peer, <my cell>, 1, op=AtomicAdd)
154	    for src  != my_rank: wait  (signal, <src cell>, g,   cmp=Ge)
155	
156	Epilogue:  for src != my_rank:
157	               notify(signal, my_rank, <src cell>, -N, op=AtomicAdd)
158	```
159	
160	`AtomicAdd` turns each cell into a credit counter: every notify is a
161	producer's `+1`, and the epilogue is the sole consumer's `-N`. Because adds
162	and subtracts are atomic and commutative, the signal is provably all-zero
163	again once every rank has finished its epilogue for a call — **the signal
164	carries no state that outlives one call**, so every call's generation `g`
165	restarts at 1 and no cross-call bookkeeping is required. A slow rank can
166	inflate a fast rank's own next-call credit by at most 1 while it finishes the
167	current call (bounded skew), so the counter never overflows and a fast rank
168	can never observe a spurious pass.
169	
170	`Ge` (not `Eq`) is load-bearing: a fast peer can advance a cell past the value
171	the waiting rank is looking for before that rank ever polls it, so an
172	equality wait would never unblock. For the same reason `Set` must never be
173	mixed with `AtomicAdd` on the same cells — a set could clobber an already
174	advanced counter.
175	
176	`N` (the credit total the epilogue subtracts) may be a **runtime scalar** —
177	`pld.system.notify`'s `value` only requires `ScalarType` — so a mesh
178	allreduce's per-chunk credit count does not need to be known at compile time.
179	
180	**Constraints:**
181	
182	| Constraint | Why |
183	| ---------- | --- |
184	| One signal must not be shared between mesh (`[NR, 1]`) and ring (`[2*(NR-1), NR]`) allreduce | Mesh addresses `[rank, 0]`; ring addresses `[row, rank]` — a shape mismatch, checked at lowering time |
185	| A call aborted mid-flight (error / timeout) leaves the signal non-zero | Credits leak; recover via a host-side reset (`reset_persistent_windows`) before the next dispatch |
186	
187	Because the protocol is call-local and the signal always starts a call at
188	all-zero, collectives are legal inside `for` / `while` / `if` — each call is a
189	closed cycle, so the same compile-time `expected` values are reused every
190	iteration. The only remaining requirement is rank-uniform execution (inherent
191	to any barrier): rank-divergent control flow deadlocks, surfaced by `TWAIT`'s
192	spin-count assert.
193	
194	## Op reference
195	
196	### `pld.tile.remote_load` (TLOAD)
197	
198	```text
199	pld.tile.remote_load(target, peer, offsets, shape[, valid_shape])
200	    -> TileType(shape, target.dtype)
201	```
202	
203	Reads a region of the `peer` rank's slice of a window-bound `DistributedTensor`
204	into a local tile. Mirrors `tile.load` at the IR level (positional `offsets` /
205	`shape` tuples, `TileType` result) but the source is a *remote* slice — the
206	address translation is realised at codegen by inline peer-offset arithmetic
207	over the `CommContext` + `addptr` + `make_tensor_view`.
208	
209	`valid_shape` is optional. With or without it, type inference intersects the
210	requested window with the source tensor's effective valid region and checks
211	provable physical bounds. When present, `shape` remains the physical UB tile
212	allocation while `valid_shape` additionally limits the remote partition and
213	the tile's valid extent. This is the fixed-width ragged-tail form used by
214	chunked collectives.
215	
216	Every symbolic source or requested valid extent that survives inference must
217	be runtime-bound by a kernel scalar, loop variable, or physical tensor-shape
218	parameter. A symbol that appears only in type metadata is rejected during PTO
219	codegen.
220	
221	Verifier: `target` must be `DistributedTensorType`; `peer` must be a
222	`ScalarType` rank index; `offsets` / `shape` / optional `valid_shape` must each
223	be a `MakeTuple` whose rank equals `target.shape.size()`.
224	
225	DSL (`python/pypto/language/distributed/op/tile_ops.py`) accepts positional or
226	keyword arguments; the IR op keeps them positional, matching `tile.load`.
227	
228	### `pld.tile.remote_store` / `pld.tensor.remote_store` (TSTORE)
229	
230	```text
231	pld.tile.remote_store(src_tile, target, peer, offsets, *, atomic: int = 0) -> Unknown
232	pld.tensor.remote_store(src, target, peer, offsets, *, atomic: int = 0) -> Unknown
233	```
234	
235	Writes a local value into a region of the `peer` rank's slice of a window-bound
236	`DistributedTensor`. Mirrors `tile.store` at the IR level (positional `offsets`
237	tuple, optional `atomic` attr, side-effect-only return) but the destination is a
238	*remote* slice — address translation happens at codegen via inline peer-offset
239	arithmetic over the `CommContext` + `addptr` + `make_tensor_view`.
240	
241	The two forms differ **only** in the IR level of `src`; `pld.remote_store`
242	dispatches on the operand, so user code reads the same at either level.
243	
244	Verifier (both forms):
245	
246	| Rule | Note |
247	| ---- | ---- |
248	| `target` is `DistributedTensorType`, `peer` a `ScalarType` rank index | |
249	| `offsets` is a `MakeTuple` of rank `target.shape.size()` | |
250	| `src.dtype == target.dtype`, `target` rank ≥ 2 | |
251	| `src` is 2-D, or N-D with every leading dim 1 | the deducer runs *before* `FlattenTileNdTo2D` collapses N-D tiles; a leading extent > 1 would fold into the row count and overrun the target |
252	| the pushed region fits inside `target` at `offsets` (static dims only) | `remote_store` has no transfer `shape` to clamp against — the extent comes from `src`, so without this an oversized push silently overwrote the peer's neighbouring region |
253	| `src` is `TileType` (tile form) / `TensorType` (tensor form) | each diagnostic names the sibling entry point, so the author lands on the one for their level |
254	
255	Lowering (tensor form): `ConvertTensorToTileOps` rewrites it 1:1 to the tile
256	form via `RegisterSimple`. Its `InputSpaceReq{Vec}` makes the op *total* on its
257	argument surface — `BridgeInputSpaces` only rewrites `TensorType` operands, so a
258	computed value (already a tile) passes straight through keeping its space, while
259	a GM-resident `src` is auto-bridged with a natural `tile.load` into Vec.
260	
261	Codegen: the tile is 2-D (height × width) after the tile pipeline; the emitted
262	`pto.partition_view` has `target`'s rank with the leading `(target.rank - 2)`
263	dims set to size 1 (matching `notify`'s `one_dims(rank, "1")`). A 2-D push
264	therefore lands on the inner two dims of any N-D peer slice (N ≥ 2) without the
265	caller reshaping — and guards the older codegen that emitted a fixed-2D
266	`partition_view` regardless of target rank.
267	
268	`atomic = AtomicType.kAdd` appends `{atomicType = #pto<atomic_type atomic_add>}`
269	to the `pto.tstore`, making the push a **combine** (`peer_region += src`) — the
270	cross-rank twin of `tile.store`'s split-K accumulation, and what an all-to-all
271	combine needs. Emitted only for `kAdd`, so plain pushes stay byte-identical.
272	`kAdd` requires an fp32/bf16/fp16/int32/int16/int8 dtype -- the same hardware
273	allow-list `tile.store` enforces -- and bf16 carries the same Ascend910B-only
274	restriction on top.
275	
276	`pld.tensor.put` (TPUT) has **no** tile-source form — its staging tile is a
277	bounce buffer, not a data source. Pushing a computed value is `remote_store`'s
278	job; pushing a bulk GM region that need not fit on-core is `put`'s.
279	
280	DSL (`python/pypto/language/distributed/op/tile_ops.py`,
281	`.../tensor_ops.py`) exposes `target` / `peer` / `offsets` as
282	positional-or-keyword for readability and round-tripping; the IR ops keep them
283	positional, matching `tile.store`.
284	
285	### `pld.tensor.put` (TPUT)
286	
287	```text
288	pld.tensor.put(dst, peer, src, *, atomic: int,
289	               chunk_rows: int = 0, chunk_cols: int = 0, pipeline: bool = False) -> Unknown
290	pld.tensor.put(dst, peer, src, dst_offsets, src_offsets, shape,
291	               *, atomic: int, chunk_rows: int = 0, chunk_cols: int = 0, pipeline: bool = False) -> Unknown
292	```
293	
294	Synchronously writes local `src` data into the `peer` rank's slice of the
295	window-bound `dst`. `dst` is a GM-level `DistributedTensor` view; `src` may be
296	either a `DistributedTensor` view *or* a plain `Tensor` — TPUT only requires a
297	readable local GM region on the source side, so kernels can push directly from
298	host-backed inputs without first staging through a window buffer. The VEC
299	staging tile is materialised by `ConvertTensorToTileOps` as an internal
300	`tile.create + pld.tile.put`, so it flows through PyPTO's memory allocator and
301	never appears on the DSL surface.
302	
303	With no offsets/shape this writes the full local `src` slice to the full peer
304	`dst` slice. Supplying `dst_offsets`, `src_offsets`, and `shape` narrows the
305	transfer to matching subregions; all three must be provided together.
306	
307	**Staging-tile chunking.** By default the staging tile spans the whole
308	flattened transfer `[rows, cols]` extent (`rows` = product of the leading dims,
309	`cols` = the innermost dim), so a transfer must fit in UB. The optional
310	`chunk_rows` / `chunk_cols` attrs (`0` = full) shrink the staging tile to a
311	sub-tile of that extent; the codegen keeps the `pto.comm.tput` partition views
312	at the **full** transfer extent and pto-isa TPUT 2-D-slides the transfer through
313	the smaller stage. This lets a single `put` move data larger than UB without the
314	caller writing an explicit chunk loop. Oversized chunk values are clamped to the
315	transfer extent.
316	
317	**Double-buffering (`pipeline`).** Setting `pipeline=True`
318	makes `ConvertTensorToTileOps` materialise **two** identical VEC staging tiles
319	(`tput_stage_ping` / `tput_stage_pong`) and thread both into `pld.tile.put` as a
320	second `stage` operand. The codegen then emits the ping-pong form
321	`pto.comm.tput(dst_pv, src_pv, buf(%ping, %pong) : …)`, which PTOAS routes to
322	pto-isa's double-buffered `TPUT` overload — it overlaps the TLOAD of the next
323	chunk with the TSTORE of the previous one across the two tiles. Because the
324	benefit only exists when the transfer is chunked into more than one piece,
325	`pipeline` **requires both `chunk_rows` and `chunk_cols` to be set** (the deducer
326	and the DSL both reject `pipeline` without a full chunk). The two tiles are
327	distinct `tile.create` allocations, so the memory allocator gives them
328	non-overlapping UB addresses (pto-isa's ping/pong requirement).
329	
330	**Dynamic transfer extent.** The transfer may be **dynamic** — either the
331	subregion `shape` (a runtime sub-extent of the window) or the `dst` / `src`
332	window (`DistributedTensorType`) dims themselves, for a full-slice transfer.
333	pto-isa reads the extent from the partition views at runtime, so the codegen
334	emits a dynamic partition view (`<?x…>`) and chunks it. A dynamic flattened
335	transfer dim must be bounded by the corresponding static chunk, because the VEC
336	staging tile is statically allocated: a dynamic innermost dim requires
337	`chunk_cols`, a dynamic leading dim requires `chunk_rows`. For a full-slice
338	transfer the `dst` and `src` dims must match — by value when static, structurally
339	when dynamic.
340	
341	Verifier: `dst` must be `DistributedTensorType`; `src` must be either
342	`TensorType` or `DistributedTensorType` (matched via `AsTensorTypeLike`);
343	`peer` must be a `ScalarType`; `dst` and `src` must share element type, rank,
344	and **positive** dimensions (positivity checked on static dims; dynamic dims are
345	allowed and bounded by the chunk). Full-slice `put` requires matching `dst` /
346	`src` shape; subregion `put` allows different full slice extents as long as the
347	explicit transfer region is in bounds (checked on static dims). Any dynamic
348	transfer dim requires a matching static chunk (see above). `atomic` selects
349	overwrite vs atomic-add (see `AtomicType`). `atomic=Add` additionally requires a
350	`FP32/BF16/FP16/INT32/INT16/INT8` destination (the hardware atomic-add dtypes,
351	since TPUT lands its chunks through the same store pipe as `tile.store`); a
352	`BF16` destination is further restricted to the Ascend910B (A2/A3) profile by the
353	`AtomicAddDtypeValid` property verifier. The lowered `pld.tile.put` verifier
354	requires the staging tile to **fit within** the flattened transfer in both
355	**static** dims (it may be smaller — a chunk — but never larger; dynamic dims
356	are bounded by the chunk at runtime).
357	
358	### `pld.tensor.get` (TGET)
359	
360	```text
361	pld.tensor.get(dst, peer, src, *, chunk_rows: int = 0, chunk_cols: int = 0, pipeline: bool = False) -> Unknown
362	pld.tensor.get(dst, peer, src, dst_offsets, src_offsets, shape,
363	               *, chunk_rows: int = 0, chunk_cols: int = 0, pipeline: bool = False) -> Unknown
364	```
365	
366	Synchronously reads the `peer` rank's slice of the window-bound `src` into the
367	local `dst`. `dst` may be a window-bound `DistributedTensor` or a plain
368	`Tensor`; `src` must be a window-bound `DistributedTensor`. The VEC staging
369	tile is materialised by `ConvertTensorToTileOps` as an internal
370	`tile.create + pld.tile.get`, so it flows through PyPTO's memory allocator and
371	never appears on the DSL surface.
372	
373	With no offsets/shape this reads the full peer `src` slice into the full local
374	`dst` slice. Supplying `dst_offsets`, `src_offsets`, and `shape` narrows the
375	transfer to matching subregions; all three must be provided together. The
376	optional `chunk_rows` / `chunk_cols` attrs (`0` = full) shrink the staging tile
377	to a sub-tile of the flattened transfer extent so pto-isa TGET auto-chunks the
378	full transfer through it — same contract as `put` above, including a **dynamic
379	transfer** (the subregion `shape` or the full-slice `dst` / `src` window dims)
380	bounded by a matching static chunk (dynamic innermost needs `chunk_cols`,
381	dynamic leading needs `chunk_rows`). Setting `pipeline=True`
382	double-buffers the chunked read through two staging tiles
383	(`tget_stage_ping` / `tget_stage_pong`), emitting
384	`pto.comm.tget(…, buf(%ping, %pong) : …)` for pto-isa's ping-pong `TGET`
385	overload — same contract as `put`, and likewise **requires both `chunk_rows` and
386	`chunk_cols`**.
387	
388	Verifier: `dst` must be either `TensorType` or `DistributedTensorType` (matched
389	via `AsTensorTypeLike`); `src` must be `DistributedTensorType`; `peer` must be a
390	`ScalarType`; `dst` and `src` must share element type, rank, and **positive**
391	dimensions (positivity checked on static dims; dynamic dims allowed, bounded by
392	the chunk). Full-slice `get` requires matching `dst` / `src` shape; subregion
393	`get` allows different full slice extents as long as the explicit transfer
394	region is in bounds (checked on static dims); any dynamic transfer dim requires
395	a matching static chunk. Besides `chunk_rows` / `chunk_cols`, `get` accepts no
396	keyword attributes.
397	
398	### `pld.tensor.all_to_all_v`
399	
400	```text
401	pld.tensor.all_to_all_v(
402	    input, target, signal, send_counts, recv_counts
403	) -> DistributedTensorType(target)
404	```
405	
406	Variable-size all-to-all (MPI_Alltoallv). Flat 2D layouts:
407	
408	- `input` — Tensor or DistributedTensor `[NR*MAX_RECV, SIZE]`
409	- `target` — DistributedTensor `[NR*MAX_RECV, SIZE]` (window-as-result)
410	- `signal` — DistributedTensor INT32 `[NR, 1]` (self-clearing credit barrier; reusable across calls)
411	- `send_counts` — Tensor-like INT32 `[NR]` or `[NR, 1]` (runtime rows per dest)
412	- `recv_counts` — DistributedTensor INT32 `[NR, 1]` (InOut recvcounts)
413	
414	`MAX_RECV = target.shape[0] // NR`. Lowering reads `send_counts[dest]` at
415	runtime, clamps to `MAX_RECV`, and publishes the **clamped** count into peer
416	`recv_counts[my_rank, 0]` via `pld.system.notify` (Set). The push itself
417	always transfers the full `MAX_RECV`-row capacity block per destination —
418	independent of the runtime count — so rows beyond a sender's actual count
419	still cross the wire; after the barrier the receiver uses `recv_counts[src, 0]`
420	to skip those rows (MPI_Alltoallv semantics apply to the logical result, not
421	the wire transfer). On the InCore path the transfer is a compile-time-sized
422	`pld.tile.put` (PTOAS requires static partition-view dims); on the HOST path
423	the kernel derives `MAX_RECV` at entry from the runtime rank count
424	(`target.shape[0] / nranks`), so it is always consistent with the devices
425	actually running.
426	
427	**InCore composite** (`LowerCompositeOps`): the primitive above, decomposed
428	into `pld.tile.put` + `pld.system.notify`/`wait` inside a chip kernel.
429	
430	**HOST builtin** (`LowerHostTensorCollectives`): the same 5-arg call, made
431	from a `host_orch` function, lowers per-device to `builtin.tensor.all_to_all_v`
432	— an in-kernel-TPUT AIV builtin following the same pattern as
433	`builtin.tensor.all_to_all`. `input` and `send_counts` must both be
434	window-bound `DistributedTensor`s at this layer (narrower than the composite's
435	`AsTensorTypeLike`, forced by the HOST dispatch codegen, which only supports
436	window-bound or tile args) — all five operands (`input`, `target`, `signal`,
437	`send_counts`, `recv_counts`) must resolve to pairwise-distinct window
438	allocations (aliasing any pair is a cross-process race: data-vs-data is a TPUT
439	overwrite, data-vs-control is a notify/count write racing a kernel read,
440	control-vs-control is a notify racing a count publish). The kernel derives
441	`MAX_RECV` at entry as `target.shape[0] / nranks` (the runtime comm-domain
442	size), so the block layout is always consistent with the devices actually
443	running — no exact `signal.shape[0]` == device-count requirement and no
444	per-`MAX_RECV` variant mangling. Not supported inside a `for`/`while` loop in
445	`host_orch` (single-use signal protocol) — the same restriction
446	`LowerCompositeOps` enforces on the InCore path.
447	
448	### `pld.tensor.allreduce`
449	
450	```text
451	pld.tensor.allreduce(src, *, op: ReduceOp = ReduceOp.Sum, mode: str = "mesh", core_num: int = 1) -> DistributedTensorType(src)
452	pld.tensor.allreduce(src, signal, *, op: ReduceOp = ReduceOp.Sum, mode: str = "mesh", core_num: int = 1) -> DistributedTensorType(src)
453	```
454	
455	Reduces every participating rank's window-bound `src` slice in place and returns
456	the same type as `src`. The `mode` keyword selects the lowering algorithm:
457	
458	Fully-valid packed mesh targets are viewed as one logical `[1, N]` stream and
459	processed in UB chunks of at most 16 KiB. A statically known `N` smaller than
460	that budget shrinks the physical chunk to the smallest 32-byte-aligned width
461	that covers `N`; larger or dynamic inputs retain the maximum width. The last
462	chunk keeps its selected physical width
463	but carries `valid_shape=[1, min(chunk, N-offset)]`, so arbitrary element counts
464	neither read nor store past the end.
465	
466	For mesh lowering, a partial `TensorView.valid_shape` is preserved for packed ND
467	targets when its valid box can be represented by collapsing the leading dimensions
468	to one 2D rectangle and a statically bounded physical tile fits within one 16-KiB
469	chunk. A symbolic valid extent falls back to the source's physical rectangle when
470	that rectangle fits the budget. Oversized partial rectangles,
471	strided targets, DN partial views, and non-representable partial boxes are rejected
472	explicitly.
473	
474	Any symbolic target or partial-valid extent that survives lowering must be
475	runtime-bound by a kernel scalar, loop variable, or physical tensor-shape
476	parameter; a type-metadata-only symbol is rejected during PTO codegen. A fully
477	dynamic physical target dimension is bound from that tensor parameter.
478	
479	- **`"mesh"` (default)** — direct all-to-all exchange with O(P) HCCL windows.
480	  Signal shape `[NR, 1]` (one cell per rank). A ready barrier (generation 1)
481	  precedes the chunk loop. Each chunk performs `remote_load+accumulate`, then
482	  a barrier on its own call-local generation before store-back, preventing
483	  write-after-read races. A self-clearing epilogue then subtracts the call's
484	  total credit count back out of every cell (see
485	  [Barrier-signal protocol](#barrier-signal-protocol)), so the signal is
486	  all-zero again once the call completes.
487	- **`"ring"`** — NCCL-style chunked reduce-scatter + allgather schedule with
488	  O(1) HCCL windows.  Signal shape `[2 * (NR − 1), NR]` (one row per ring
489	  round, one cell per rank). A packed ND target is viewed as one logical
490	  `[1, SIZE]` stream; a partial valid box must be a contiguous row-major
491	  prefix. Lowering keeps the full physical
492	  `[1, product(target.shape)]` view and records the logical prefix as
493	  `TensorView.valid_shape=[1, product(target.valid_shape)]`. FP32 divides
494	  `SIZE` with balanced `floor(i * SIZE / NR)` boundaries. FP16 rounds each
495	  interior boundary up to 16 elements (32 bytes) and caps it at `SIZE`, so
496	  every non-empty segment begins at an MTE-safe address without changing the
497	  packed user-visible layout. Empty segments remain legal for very short
498	  inputs. Each segment is processed in at most 16-KiB physical subchunks; an
499	  FP16 ragged remote tail rounds only its physical read span to 32 bytes and
500	  restores the logical `valid_shape` before reduction or store. Every
501	  subchunk uses ready and read-complete barriers on its own call-local
502	  generation before store-back, preventing write-after-read races. A
503	  self-clearing epilogue subtracts the call's total credit count back out of
504	  every row of the signal afterward.
505	
506	Host-orchestrator user code may omit `signal` outside `for` and `while` loops;
507	the [`SynthesizeAllReduceSignals`](passes/40-synthesize_allreduce_signals.md)
508	pass inserts a private INT32 signal window with semantic shape
509	`[world_size, core_num]`
510	for that call (mesh mode only — `mode="ring"` requires an explicit signal). The
511	pass binds `world_size = pld.world_size()` as a standalone statement and uses
512	that variable in the synthesized buffer size and window shape. The
513	self-clearing protocol (see [Barrier-signal protocol](#barrier-signal-protocol))
514	makes every call a stateless cycle, so calls inside `for` / `while` loops are
515	supported like any other collective. Explicit
516	`signal` remains the internal form used by InCore lowering and by tests that
517	intentionally construct the internal protocol. Comm-domain materialisation then
518	keeps the signal buffer in the same domain as `src`, even when it is not passed
519	to a user chip kernel. Mesh, ring, and host-builtin paths support FP16 and FP32
520	with `ReduceOp.Sum`, `Max`, `Min`, and `Prod` for arbitrary positive element
521	counts. InCore lowering uses UB-bounded chunks; the host builtin uses
522	256-element chunks. InCore mesh and ring round only the physical FP16 remote
523	tail span to 32 bytes. The host builtin rounds ragged FP16 and FP32 load spans
524	to 32 bytes. Both preserve the logical valid shape. The host builtin accepts
525	either a rank-1 `[world_size]` signal or a rank-2
526	`[world_size, signal_stride]` signal. Ring mode (`mode="ring"`) for the host
527	orchestrator lowers to `builtin.tensor.allreduce_ring` and requires an explicit
528	rank-2 `[2 * (NR - 1) + 1, NR]` INT32 signal (one extra row for the return
529	barrier).
530	
531	#### Host multi-core AllReduce (`core_num`)
532	
533	`core_num` selects how many AIV blocks one HOST `pld.tensor.allreduce` dispatch
534	uses **on each rank**. It does not change the task hierarchy: `device=r` still
535	selects the card and the call still lowers to one builtin orchestration task per
536	rank; that task now launches a synchronized SPMD grid of `core_num` blocks.
537	
538	```python
539	data = pld.tensor.allreduce(data, signal, op=pld.ReduceOp.Sum, core_num=4)
540	```
541	
542	| Constraint | Rule |
543	| ---------- | ---- |
544	| Range | Positive compile-time integer, default `1` (pre-existing behavior) |
545	| Schedule | Mesh only — `mode="ring"` requires `core_num == 1` |
546	| Capacity | At most the backend's AIV core count (submitted via `rt_submit_aiv_task`, so one block = one AIV core) |
547	| InCore | Must stay `1`; use an enclosing `pl.spmd(...)` for multi-core work |
548	
549	**Signal layout.** The signal is a peer-major, lane-contiguous
550	`[world_size, signal_stride]` matrix with `signal_stride >= core_num`. Block `b`
551	waits on `signal_base + peer * signal_stride + b` and notifies peer `p` at
552	`signal_base + my_rank * signal_stride + b`, so every `(peer, block)` pair owns
553	an independent counter. A rank-1 `[world_size]` signal (stride 1) is valid only
554	for `core_num == 1`. A synthesized signal is exactly `[world_size, core_num]`;
555	an explicit signal may be wider.
556	
557	**Kernel partitioning.** Blocks own 256-element tiles block-cyclically — block
558	`b` processes tiles `b, b + C, b + 2C, ...` for `C` launched blocks — so no two
559	blocks touch the same chunk. Each block runs the ready barrier once, then a
560	read-done barrier per chunk. That per-chunk barrier must stay **before** the
561	store: without it a rank could overwrite its source chunk before the matching
562	block on another rank has remote-loaded it. Blocks with no data still run the
563	ready barrier, keeping ranks symmetric and letting `core_num` exceed the chunk
564	count. Blocks at or beyond `signal_stride` have no lane to own, so they retire
565	immediately without joining the barrier; `signal_stride` is equal on every rank,
566	so all ranks retire the same blocks and the protocol stays symmetric.
567	
568	**Why one SPMD grid rather than `pl.parallel`.** `pl.parallel(N)` emits `N`
569	independent tasks, each with its own TaskId and scheduling lifetime — unsafe for
570	an in-place collective. Ranks may schedule chunk tasks in different orders, so a
571	task waiting on another rank's matching chunk can deadlock, and conservative
572	dependency tracking on the shared InOut window tends to serialize them anyway.
573	One SPMD grid avoids both: `require_sync_start` admits all blocks together and
574	`block_idx` gives deterministic, matching partitioning on every rank. That is a
575	per-card admission guarantee, not a global simultaneous start across ranks — the
576	ready barrier absorbs cross-rank launch skew.
577	
578	### `pld.system.notify` (TNOTIFY)
579	
580	```text
581	pld.system.notify(target, peer, offsets, value, *, op: int) -> Unknown
582	```
583	
584	Writes `value` into the `peer` rank's signal slot of `target` (a window-bound
585	`DistributedTensor`, typically a 1-D INT32 "signal matrix"). `op` selects
586	atomic-add vs set (see `NotifyOp`).
587	
588	Verifier: `target` must be `DistributedTensorType`; `peer` and `value` must be
589	`ScalarType`; `offsets` must be a `MakeTuple` of rank equal to the target rank.
590	
591	### `pld.system.wait` (TWAIT)
592	
593	```text
594	pld.system.wait(signal, offsets, expected, *, cmp: int) -> Unknown
595	```
596	
597	Blocks until this rank's own signal slot of `signal` satisfies the `cmp`
598	predicate against `expected` (see `WaitCmp`).
599	
600	Verifier: `signal` must be `DistributedTensorType`; `expected` must be
601	`ScalarType`; `offsets` must be a `MakeTuple` of rank equal to the signal rank.
602	
603	### `pld.system.defer_wait` (Simpler deferred completion)
604	
605	Signature: `pld.system.defer_wait(signal, offsets, expected, *, cmp: int) -> Unknown`.
606	
607	Registers a local counter condition without `pto.comm.twait`. The kernel can retire and
608	release its AIV, but Simpler delays the ordinary TaskId's completion until every condition
609	is ready; the kernel is never resumed.
610	
611	V1 accepts a direct window-bound INT32 `DistributedTensor` parameter with ND/DN
612	addressing, integer/index offsets and threshold, and only `WaitCmp::kGe`.
613	Slices/views/SSA aliases, NZ layout, and rank-zero signals are rejected. Counter
614	storage is INT32 but polling is unsigned `>=`: thresholds and published values must
615	remain monotonic in `[0, INT32_MAX]`; `-1` appears as `UINT32_MAX` and falsely
616	satisfies. One task may register at most 64 conditions, independent of the scheduler's
617	64-concurrent-deferred-task limit.
618	
619	The scope outliner requires a dedicated top-level single-block pure-AIV `pl.at(CORE_GROUP)`
620	waiter with no predicate or `allow_early_resolve=True`.
621	Pure scalar work may occur between registrations, but `tensor.read`,
622	payload/cache operations, and other communication cannot. Scalars carried across
623	a branch merge or a loop iteration are such bookkeeping — the SSA phi / iter_arg
624	yields `ConvertToSSA` inserts for them are accepted, and a loop that registers no
625	condition is allowed and needs no statically known trip count. A terminal waiter with no
626	continuation may be submitted fire-and-forget and need not capture a TaskId. An
627	unmarked direct `@pl.jit.incore` / AIV use is rejected because it bypasses the
628	validated single-block task launch and runtime `AsyncCtx` contract. Programmatically
629	constructed IR carrying the internal waiter marker is accepted only after the full
630	body and orchestration call-site contract is revalidated.
631	
632	Continuation uses ordinary `deps=[wait_tid]`; there is no second dependency type.
633	Simpler withholds the normal TaskId fanout until the counter is ready. Its standard
634	task-start cache invalidation then runs on the normally dispatched consumer. The
635	producer must still make payload writes visible before publishing the signal, and
636	the waiter must remain ineligible for early resolve so consumer pickup cannot precede readiness.
637	
638	Codegen passes checked flattened offsets and raw dispatch arguments to an adapter that
639	registers a counter `CompletionToken` in `AsyncCtx`. The legacy
640	`pld.system.wait`/`pto.comm.twait` path is unchanged. See the
641	[distributed primitives guide](../user/distributed/02-primitives.md#deferred-completion-release-the-core-keep-the-task-pending)
642	for the complete programming contract and examples.
643	
644	## Shared codegen infrastructure
645	
646	The low-level RMA and synchronization ops lower through PTO codegen helpers in
647	`src/backend/common/pto_ops_distributed.cpp` and `src/codegen/pto/pto_codegen.cpp`.
648	The reusable pieces — shared so each op's lowering carries no bespoke peer
649	arithmetic — are:
650	
651	| Helper | Role |
652	| ------ | ---- |
653	| `PTOCodegen::EmitCommRemoteOffsetInline` | emits the `CommContext` reads + byte-to-element division **inline** in the caller's own `func.func`, turning `(ctx, peer)` into the element offset of the peer's window slice. No module-level helper is emitted: a mixed cube+vector group is one MLIR module holding both the AIC and the AIV function, and a helper carrying no `pto.kernel_kind` strands its value-returning `return` outside PTOAS's `__DAV_VEC__` section guard |
654	| `EmitCommRemoteView` | emits the inline peer offset + `addptr` + `make_tensor_view` at the call site, yielding the peer-addressed view (used by `remote_load`, `get`'s `src`, and `put`'s `dst`) |
655	| `EmitPartitionViewPTO` | wraps a tensor view in a full-slice `partition_view` with given offsets/sizes (used by every op for both local and peer operands) |
656	| `ResolveDistTensorBinding` | resolves a `DistributedTensor` arg to its codegen binding (type + window var) |
657	| `AsTensorTypeLike` | kind-trait downcast accepting both `TensorType` and `DistributedTensorType` where a view's element/shape info is read uniformly |
658	
659	The local-vs-remote split is intentional: a *local* PTO operand (e.g. `get`'s
660	`dst`, `put`'s `src`, `wait`'s `signal`) reuses the tensor view already created
661	by `EmitMakeTensorViews` with no peer arithmetic, while a *remote* operand (e.g.
662	`remote_load`'s `target`, `get`'s `src`, `put`'s `dst`) goes through
663	`EmitCommRemoteView`. `defer_wait` is also local, but its adapter receives the
664	direct parameter base plus a checked flattened logical element offset rather
665	than a PTO tensor view.
666	
667	## Pipeline integration
668	
669	Comm domains and their slot allocations are materialised by the
670	[`MaterializeCommDomainScopes`](passes/41-materialize_comm_domain_scopes.md) pass, which wraps each
671	host_orch body in nested `CommDomainScopeStmt` nodes (one per inferred comm domain) and produces the
672	per-window `WindowBuffer` records that the runtime binds physical buffers to.
673	Host-level tensor collectives are then lowered by
674	[`LowerHostTensorCollectives`](passes/42-lower_host_tensor_collectives.md) into internal builtin chip
675	dispatches before the final `Simplify`.
676	
677	## Testing
678	
679	- **IR / parser**: `tests/ut/ir/parser/test_remote_load.py`,
680	  `tests/ut/ir/parser/test_remote_store.py`, `test_system_ops.py`,
681	  `test_get_op.py`, `test_put_op.py`, plus the negative verifier coverage
682	  in `tests/ut/ir/test_distributed_ops.py`.
683	- **Codegen**: `tests/ut/codegen/distributed/test_distributed_pto_codegen.py`.
684	- **End-to-end (ST)**: `tests/st/distributed/test_l3_allreduce.py` (mesh
685	  allreduce with dynamic rank dim `NR = pl.dynamic("NR")`; **P=2** default,
686	  **P=4** on any four devices (e.g. `--device=0,1,2,3` or `--device=0-3`)),
687	  `test_l3_allgather.py`, `test_l3_reduce_scatter.py`, `test_l3_broadcast.py`
688	  (each likewise dynamic-NR, P=2/P=4),
689	  `test_l3_tensor_allreduce_intrinsic.py`, `test_l3_tensor_allreduce_ring_intrinsic.py`,
690	  `test_l3_allreduce_ring.py` (hand-rolled ring RS+AG), `test_l3_host_tensor_allreduce.py`,
691	  `test_l3_host_tensor_allreduce_ring.py`,
692	  `test_l3_ep_dispatch_combine.py`, `test_l3_notify_wait.py`,
693	  `test_l3_tensor_all_to_all_v_intrinsic.py` (InCore composite),
694	  `test_l3_host_tensor_all_to_all_v.py` (HOST builtin), and related L3 STs
695	  under `tests/st/distributed/`. **Put/get canonical e2e contracts** are now
696	  enabled: `test_l3_put.py` (ring overwrite, row-offset put, atomic-add put, and
697	  chunked/pipelined transfers ✅), `test_l3_get.py` (ring read, row-offset get ✅),
698	  and `test_l3_remote_store.py` (tile-level subview push ✅, plus a
699	  tensor-level push of a *computed* value ✅). Deferred completion is covered by
700	  `test_l3_deferred_completion.py`: A2/A3 AIV-saturation/core-release,
701	  already-ready registration reuse, A5 cross-rank correctness, persistent
702	  monotonic epochs, and ordinary TaskId dependency gating. Other communication
703	  STs use the `pld.system.notify` / `pld.system.wait` handshake pattern
704	  established by notify/wait and collective STs.
